original.target_description: Published Trull & Sher (1994), single nonclinical young-adult cohort at Wave 4. Multiple regression predicting NEO-FFI Neuroticism from gender and simultaneous lifetime diagnoses of any substance use disorder, any anxiety disorder, and major depression; target coefficient is for major depression. Openness corresponds to the supplied open-mindedness description; Neuroticism corresponds to negative emotionality.

n.sample_role: Young-adult participants; 468 assessed at Wave 4, but analytic N is not explicitly stated for the target multiple regression.
n.exclusions: 490 originally enrolled; 468 assessed at Wave 4. Target-regression-specific exclusions or missingness not reported.
n.location: p. 351, Method; p. 355 (PDF p. 6), Analyses Controlling for Comorbidity
n.quote: A total of 490 subjects were originally entered into the prospective arm of the study, and 468 of these subjects (95.5%) were assessed at Wave 4.

es.location: p. 355 (PDF p. 6), Analyses Controlling for Comorbidity, multiple-regression results paragraph

p.location: p. 355 (PDF p. 6), Analyses Controlling for Comorbidity, same multiple-regression coefficient

replication.target_description: Unassigned replication side; not examined under original-only blind validation.

notes: Original-only fresh blind validation. Source version: published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service; title and author match verified in supplied primary text. Quotes preserve OCR notation for beta, signs and spacing; es.value transcribes the printed coefficient. These are coefficients for diagnoses predicting personality while controlling diagnostic comorbidity, not logistic-regression coefficients predicting diagnosis. Tables 3 and 4 report N for different logistic regressions and are not used to assign analytic N to this target regression. No conversion performed. Replication and reported success intentionally unexamined.
